question: What is the main danger of unsafe injection practices?
explanation: Unsafe injections often involve contaminated equipment, which can directly transfer infectious agents into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h1)

question: Why should patients be encouraged to ask questions about their injections?

options.A: It reduces the administrative workload of the hospital records unit
options.B: It lowers the financial cost of purchasing disposable syringes
options.C: Hospital management requires patients to audit drug expiration dates
options.D: Patients act as a vital safety barrier against clinical errors

explanation: Active patient participation creates an extra layer of defense against accidental mistakes during medication administration. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h1)

question: What cultural attitude often stops patients from asking healthcare workers safety questions?

options.A: Assuming that all treatments are fully funded by the government
options.B: Believing that nurses only handle administrative ward duties
options.C: Expecting doctors to share personal medical histories freely
options.D: Viewing providers as absolute authorities who cannot be questioned

explanation: Deep-seated respect for medical authority creates a power imbalance that makes patients hesitant to ask questions. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h2)

question: How does a strict medical hierarchy affect how patients communicate during procedures?

options.A: It encourages patients to demand detailed pharmacological breakdowns
options.B: It motivates patients to cross-check medical charts independently
options.C: It discourages patients from voicing concerns about sterile injection tools
options.D: It forces clinicians to explain every single step of the procedure

explanation: When patients feel intimidated by medical authority, they are less likely to speak up about infection control issues. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h2)

question: What usually happens when a patient has low health literacy regarding injections?

options.A: Inspecting disposal boxes before any drug administration
options.B: Demanding brand-name oral medications instead of injections
options.C: Failing to recognize unsterile or hazardous equipment
options.D: Reporting minor clinical delays to hospital administration

explanation: Without basic education on safety standards, patients cannot easily spot dangerous infection control breaches. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h3)

question: What is a main reason a patient might miss seeing a reused syringe in a busy ward?

options.A: Excessive trust in the cleanliness of hospital floors
options.B: Lack of knowledge about proper sterile packaging and disposal
options.C: Confusion between intravenous and intramuscular routes
options.D: Belief that all needles are manufactured self-sterilizing

explanation: Educational gaps prevent patients from knowing what a truly single-use, sterile injection setup looks like. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h3)

question: Why do many patients prefer injections over oral tablets in local communities?

options.A: Tablets are culturally associated with mild illnesses only
options.B: They believe injections offer much faster and stronger healing
options.C: Injections are significantly cheaper than standard syrups
options.D: Government clinics provide free syringes for home use

explanation: The strong belief in the superior power of injected medications drives high consumer demand for them. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h4)

question: How does wanting a very fast recovery affect a patient's safety habits?

options.A: It blinds patients to potential infection risks in their haste to heal
options.B: It encourages patients to inspect medication batch numbers closely
options.C: It leads to a decrease in overall hospital admission rates
options.D: It forces nurses to follow strict international sterilization guidelines

explanation: The urgent desire to get better quickly often causes people to overlook dangerous shortcuts in injection delivery. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h4)

question: What fear often stops hospitalized patients from reporting unsafe clinical practices?

options.A: Fear of being charged extra fees for medical supplies
options.B: Fear of facing staff hostility and receiving poor care
options.C: Fear of mandatory isolation for questioning staff
options.D: Fear of immediate discharge from the ward facility

explanation: Vulnerable patients often worry that complaining will cause staff to treat them poorly or neglect them. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h5)

question: A patient notices a nurse preparing an injection with a questionable needle but says nothing to avoid trouble. Which barrier is this?

options.A: Financial inability to purchase safe disposable kits
options.B: Absolute lack of basic health literacy about needles
options.C: Cultural preference for herbal remedies over clinics
options.D: Fear of retaliation and compromised quality of care

explanation: Suppressing safety concerns out of self-preservation stems directly from the fear of caregiver backlash. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h5)

question: Which institutional issue directly contributes to unsafe injection practices in public clinics?

options.A: Mandatory audits of all pharmaceutical supplies
options.B: Excessive availability of advanced sterile equipment
options.C: Severe shortages of single-use disposable syringes
options.D: Too many nurses on duty during night shifts

explanation: A lack of proper equipment supplies forces healthcare workers into compromised operational situations. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h6)

question: What is a common result when a clinic runs out of basic injection kits?

options.A: The hospital automatically shuts down all outpatient departments
options.B: Nurses sterilize plastic syringes using boiling water daily
options.C: Doctors completely stop prescribing any parenteral medications
options.D: Patients are sent to buy variable quality supplies from external vendors

explanation: Supply chain failures often shift the burden of buying supplies onto patients, which increases infection risks. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h6)

question: How can a nurse best help patients speak up about unsafe procedures?

options.A: By actively inviting questions and explaining injection steps clearly
options.B: By ignoring patient inquiries to maintain strict ward discipline
options.C: By delegating all patient communication tasks to junior ward maids
options.D: By demanding that patients purchase imported medical equipment

explanation: Open communication builds confidence, empowering patients to ask questions without fear. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h7)

question: A nurse notices a patient watching nervously as a medication is drawn up. What is the best first action?

options.A: Acknowledge the patient's gaze and briefly explain the sterile steps being taken
options.B: Scold the patient for staring at the medication tray without permission
options.C: Administer the injection quickly before the patient can ask questions
options.D: Cover the tray with a towel to prevent the patient from looking

explanation: Involving the patient and addressing unspoken worries helps build a safe, trusting care environment. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h7)
